scope: Diagnostic only; no production change or SDK patch.
answer: Public APIs can run queries in a dedicated worker and avoid measured page blocking, but the worker client does not acquire into the app persistent replica. Do not adopt worker-hosted offline preparation on this SDK.

environment.fixture: current application schema and permissions; selected-account viewer

ownership: XState creatingAccounts -> choosingIdentity with guarded restore/retain/create -> opening -> available.idle/observing -> draining -> stopped/failed. Subscription callback owns unsubscribe cleanup; separate leaf actors create manager, open Db, and shut down Db. No cancellation-during-open or production auth coordinator is claimed.
identity: Disposable local-first root transferred only to same-origin diagnostic worker, restored through public account helper, never logged. Volatile AccountStore controls account selection only; cold page retains the original identity in its normal store.
acquisition: 17 table ID subscriptions plus full current-user membership and grant subscriptions; same appId/env/dbName and admitted account; no finance reads in page before worker acquisition.
coldProtocol: Gracefully release all subscriptions/client, close full persistent browser including workers, reopen same profile and original identity in a page; real proxy accepts upgrades and forwards no Jazz application frames or HTTP replies.

sourceFindings: runtime/db.js isBrowserRuntime requires window and Worker; dedicated worker fails this check and uses createWithDirectConnection even with persistent driver.
runtime/default-runtime-source.js uses the same window-based test for persistent browser leases and non-durable foreground peers. The direct worker does not attach to the durable broker.
SharedWorker is undefined in all three tested dedicated-worker realms; IndexedDB and Web Locks exist, but their existence does not select the Jazz persistent browser path.

RuntimeSourcesConfig public overrides select Wasm/broker assets, not a worker attachment transport. browserWorkerPort/session and Db.createWithBrowserWorker are marked internal; no such surface was used.
Framework/session wrappers use the same createDb factory and do not supply a separate public worker-storage attachment.
limits: Performance values are one development-runtime sample per location on one desktop, not production startup improvements or supported-device budgets.
Large samples use a minimal diagnostic input rather than the app full form; main-thread frame gaps and long tasks are measured directly.
Worker sends IDs to page; full financial rows are not marshaled into UI. No valid public sync/import path for transferring its replica into page IndexedDB was established.
Local-first identity tested; external JWT/session generation coordination and production worker ownership were not implemented.
Default browser persistence uses Jazz SharedWorker. This experiment does not replace or modify that worker.

Early diagnostic harness issues (root state target, raw-secret property accidentally spread into createDb, Vite root HTML routing, evaluate argument serialization, reinsert of deleted grant) were corrected before qualified cases. Final grant recovery uses public restore; no application defect or SDK patch was hidden.
sources: installed alpha.59 package source and declarations
decision: Keep automatic broad preparation disabled. Do not build a dedicated-worker preparation owner with the current supported API. Bounded page-side preparation remains a possible separately reviewed offline-availability feature; this experiment does not make it a startup speed optimization.
